body:
`expectSingleCompletion()` uses `QCOMPARE`, which returns from *that helper function*
rather than from the test slot. When the comparison fails the slot carries on and calls
`completionSucceeded(finished)`, which indexes an empty `QSignalSpy` — out of bounds, so
the binary segfaults instead of reporting a clean failure, taking the remaining tests in
that binary with it.

Observed while running the suite on Windows (gdb backtrace):

```
FAIL!  : cancelFinishesOnceAndRunnerIsReusable() Compared values are not the same
   Actual   (finished.count()): 0
   Expected (1)               : 1
   ...test_command_line_tool_runner.cpp(42) : failure location

Thread 1 received signal SIGSEGV
#0  completionSucceeded (finished=..., index=0) at ...:49
      return finished.at(index).at(1).toBool();
#1  cancelFinishesOnceAndRunnerIsReusable () at ...:167
```

The underlying cause of that particular failure is addressed separately, but the hazard
remains: any future failure of that helper crashes the suite rather than reporting.
Guarding the accessors on `count()`, or restructuring so the check aborts the slot, would
make failures diagnosable.
title: test_command_line_tool_runner: a failed check crashes the binary instead of reporting
